notes: A conforming compiler must honor a DISABLE whose KEY value matches the system password and refuse with status 40 one whose value does not; the written-KEY behaviour is right on every probe (wrong, SPACES, case and length variants 40; the right value 00). The question is the omitted phrase. GR7 was written when the phrase was required; 1985 made it optional (obsolete list item 11) without saying what an omitted phrase does. Read literally ('honored only if literal-1 ... match the system password') a statement with no literal-1 can match no password, but the same literal reading also refuses every key-less statement on a system with no password at all, which would make the phrase 1985 just made optional mandatory everywhere; so GR7 cannot be applied word for word to a statement that omits the phrase, and the text does not decide it. What it does say is that the password facility is the implementor's: the password 'is built into the system' (implementor-defined list item 77) and the rules for when a KEY value matches it are 'not specified, thereby resulting in a situation defined by the implementor'. Precedence: GnuCOBOL 3.2 does not implement the Communication module (probe g1: 'COMMUNICATION SECTION is not implemented', the CD fields undefined); IBM Enterprise COBOL provides no Communication module; Micro Focus was not checked. So the implementor's documented choice stands: an omitted KEY phrase asks nothing and is honored (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3.3, 'The KEY phrase at COBOL-85', kb/Work PB5287). One correction is owed to that entry: it says 'CCVS-85 programs omit it', and they do not. Every ENABLE and DISABLE in CM101M, CM102M, CM103M, CM104M, CM105M, CM202M, CM303M, CM401M and DB205A writes KEY (grep of tests/nist/programs), so the entry must rest on the text's grounds above, not on CCVS. Implementor choice: Is a DISABLE (or ENABLE) that omits the KEY phrase honored against an endpoint that has a system password? Decided by the implementor: the 1985 text leaves the password facility and its matching to the implementor (§1985:p.XVII-84 obsolete item 11, §1985:p.XVII-93 item 77) and does not say what an omitted phrase does; GnuCOBOL 3.2 does not implement the module and IBM Enterprise COBOL provides none, so precedence yields nothing; WiseOwl's recorded choice (PB5287) is honored; documented in docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3.3.

next.reason: 1985: "The DISABLE statement will be honored only if literal-1 or the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 match the system password"; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the DISABLE statement; the communication module and its DISABLE statement are not carried.". No 2023 clause holds the DISABLE feature. Candidates on INSPECT, STOP, I-O status and the RECEIVE CONTINUE phrase do not cover DISABLE or its password check.
